summary: Audit log exporter missing quant_profile_id + route identifiers for quantization profile change events
description:
Request (Compliance/Security): Update the audit log export pipeline so quantization profile change events include the required identifiers for downstream compliance reporting and customer-facing audit log exports.

Context:
- Redwood recently added route-level quantization profile enablement (opt-in) with structured audit events.
- Console change history UI is showing the right details, but the exported audit log feed (S3 -> SIEM) appears to be missing key fields (quant_profile_id + route identifiers).

Why this matters:
- Enterprise customers (and internal audits) require proof of who changed performance/cost controls and what exactly changed.
- Quantization profiles can change output quality; changes must be attributable to route + profile and searchable in the SIEM.

Observed gap:
- In exported audit events for quantization changes, we see actor + timestamp + generic event_type, but not quant_profile_id/quant_profile_ref and not route identifiers (route_id/route_name).

Requirements / acceptance criteria:
1) For audit event types related to quantization profile changes (enable/disable/change ref), export must include:
   - tenant_id
   - route_id and route_name (or route_slug if that’s the canonical identifier)
   - model_id (if available at change time)
   - quant_profile_id (resolved immutable id) and quant_profile_ref (user-specified ref/alias)
   - resolution_outcome if included (applied/fallback/disabled) is nice-to-have for change events; required for runtime events is out of scope
   - actor_user_id + actor_email (or service principal) and source (console/api)
   - diff fields: before/after for quantization_profile_ref + enabled state
2) Backward compatibility: exporter should not break consumers that parse the existing schema.
3) Documentation: update the internal field catalog for the SIEM export (what fields exist and which event types include them).

Notes:
- This ticket is about the export feed and field mapping/allowlist, not about generating the audit events themselves.
- If a field isn’t available in the event payload today, call out what needs to change upstream.

Requested by: Security/Compliance (Naomi Feldman) for upcoming FalconBank audit log export review and internal controls validation.
comments: 2025-03-13 (Naomi Feldman): Pulled a sample from the exported audit log feed (Splunk index redwood_audit_prod). For event_type=route.quantization_profile.updated the payload is missing route_id and quant_profile_id. Console UI shows the route name and profile selection, so I think the event has it but exporter is dropping it.

2025-03-13 (Kevin Osei): Acknowledged. Exporter uses a per-event allowlist (flatten + select) before shipping to S3/SIEM. Likely new fields weren’t added when PR-18503 landed. I’ll confirm what the event payload contains and whether we need an exporter-only change vs upstream event schema change.

2025-03-14 (Jada Williams): The audit event payload emitted by control plane includes route_id, route_display_name, quant_profile_ref (string), and quant_profile_id (immutable) in the event ‘details’ blob. Console reads it via the change history endpoint. If SIEM export is missing those, it’s almost certainly the exporter mapping.

2025-03-14 (Marcus Lin): +1 compliance need. For FalconBank we also need actor principal and request_id/correlation_id preserved so we can tie config change to API calls during reviews. Actor is required; correlation_id is strongly preferred.

2025-03-18 (Kevin Osei): Found root cause: exporter v2 schema flattener explicitly drops nested ‘details.*’ fields unless mapped. Quantization profile fields live under details.quantization.* and details.route.* and were never added. Proposed fix: add explicit mappings for route_id, route_name, quant_profile_id, quant_profile_ref, and diff(before/after). Keep existing top-level fields unchanged. Also adding correlation_id when present.

2025-03-19 (Kevin Osei): Patch merged + deployed to prod export worker. Validated by triggering a test change in staging and verifying export JSONL includes route_id + quant_profile_id. Starting a short prod verification window (next export batch) before marking resolved.

2025-03-20 (Naomi Feldman): Verified in Splunk: fields route_id, route_name, quant_profile_id, quant_profile_ref now present for route.quantization_profile.updated events. Actor + source preserved. This unblocks the audit log export field checklist for the security review. Thanks.
investigation_notes:
Exporter behavior:
- Current audit export pipeline flattens event payloads and applies an allowlist per event_type to stabilize downstream schemas.
- Quantization profile change metadata was added under a nested ‘details’ structure (control-plane event payload), which Console consumes.
- Exporter allowlist did not include the nested quantization profile + route identifiers, so fields were silently dropped.

Impact:
- No functional impact to product behavior.
- Compliance/reporting risk: SIEM searches cannot attribute changes to specific route/profile; customer audit export completeness concerns.

Scope decision:
- Exporter-only change (field mapping) is sufficient; upstream event emission already contains required fields.
- No backfill planned; existing historical exports remain incomplete. If a backfill is required for a specific audit window, raise a separate ticket.

Verification plan:
- Trigger route quantization setting change in staging and confirm exported JSONL row contains new fields.
- Confirm prod export batch includes the same fields and does not break existing parsers (schema version unchanged).
resolution:
Updated audit log exporter field mapping/allowlist for quantization profile route-change events to include:
- route_id, route_name
- quant_profile_id (immutable), quant_profile_ref (user-facing ref)
- before/after diff for quantization settings
- correlation_id when present

Deployed to production export workers and verified in SIEM (Splunk) that new fields are searchable for event_type=route.quantization_profile.updated.

Follow-ups:
- Update internal SIEM/audit export field catalog with the new fields for quantization profile events.
- If any enterprise customer requests historical exports with these fields, open a separate backfill/attestation ticket.
next_steps: Doc update: add quant_profile_id/quant_profile_ref + route_id/route_name to audit export field catalog (owner: Kevin Osei, due: 2025-03-22).
Confirm with Support/CS whether any customer-facing audit log export templates need updates for quantization profile events (owner: Dev Patel, due: 2025-03-27).
